# Frontend conventions

React 19, TypeScript strict, Redux Toolkit with RTK Query, react-router (declarative mode), Tailwind v4, i18next. Design for the project succeeding: the server owns server state, the URL owns what a user would bookmark, and a component owns only what it renders; a copy of server data in `useState`, an effect that sets state, or a cast that silences tsc is a defect a later maintainer pays for, not a shortcut. The root AGENTS.md has the commands and hard rules; [README.md](README.md) explains the packages. Biome (`biome.base.json`) and tsc (`tsconfig.base.json`) enforce what they can; this file is what remains. `src/pages/NotesPage.tsx`, `src/pages/LoginPage.tsx`, and `src/App.tsx` are the reference for every rule below.

## Data and state

- Every server call is a hook from `src/store/api.ts` (`useXxxQuery`, `useXxxMutation`, re-exported from the generated client): no `fetch`, no `axios`, no hand-written response types, no runtime schema for API responses. A missing endpoint or field is a backend change first, then `just api-schema` and `just api-client`; never patch generated types or `@ts-expect-error` a generated call site.
- The generated per-resource tag is the invalidation contract: never call `refetch()` or dispatch `invalidateTags` after a mutation, never add a second `createApi`. Refinement (LIST plus id tags, related resources, optimistic updates in `onQueryStarted` with `patchResult.undo()`) lives only in `src/store/api.ts` via `enhanceEndpoints`; invalidation is the default and optimistic updates are for small, frequent interactions.
- Placement, in order: API data is read from the hook where it renders, never copied into `useState` or a slice, never fetched in `useEffect`; state a user would bookmark or refresh into (page, search, filter, sort, tab) is a URL search param via `useSearchParams`, passed straight into the hook arg and never mirrored into state; everything else, form fields included, is `useState`/`useReducer` until submit; a slice is only for client state every screen needs (auth is the one shipped; adding one is an ADR because `store.ts` is template-owned).
- Every rendered query handles `isLoading` (skeleton, first load only), `isError` (a persistent `role="alert"` with a translated message), and empty `data`; keep rendering `data` while `isFetching` (dim the pager); `hasNext = data?.next != null`; prefetch the next page with `usePrefetch`. Conditional queries use `skipToken`, never `skip` with a placeholder arg; `useLazyQuery` only for user-triggered reads; Suspense is for `lazy()` only (RTK Query has no Suspense hooks).
- A mutation is `await trigger(args).unwrap()` in `try/catch`, the control `disabled={isLoading}` (only while pending, never for "invalid"); it is the form's only pending and error source (never mixed with `useActionState`). `error.data` is `unknown`: narrow it with `parseApiError` from `src/store/errors.ts`, map field errors to `aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid` on the input, everything else to the `role="alert"` summary, then focus the first invalid field.
- Tokens are touched only through `authSlice` and `src/auth/tokens.ts`; logout is `dispatch(logout())` (it clears tokens, credentials, and the query cache); never call the refresh endpoint yourself, `baseApi` does it. Routes live in `App.tsx` as one `<Routes>` tree: a pathless layout route rendering `<Outlet/>` inside one `<Suspense>` and an error boundary, screens as `lazy()` at module top (`.then((m) => ({ default: m.NotesPage }))` keeps named exports), protected screens under `RequireAuth`, which redirects with `state={{ from: location }}`; navigation is `useNavigate` or `<Link>`, never `window.location`; imports from `react-router` only.
- Feature flags: `FeatureGate` (`src/flags/FeatureGate.tsx`) wraps a gated feature's route or entry point so its surface disappears while the flag is off, exactly where the backend answers 404; `useFlag(name)` is for an inline toggle inside a screen. A missing or unloaded flag is off; never call a gated endpoint from outside its gate.
- `useAppSelector` returns one field per call (`state => state.auth.access`), never the whole state or a fresh object or array; derived lists go through `createAppSelector` at module scope; `selectFromResult` returns cached references only.
- Banned forms: `connect`, hand-written reducers or action types, `createAsyncThunk` for API data, sagas, `useEffect` fetching, `redux-form`, `react-router-dom`. When in doubt read `node_modules/@reduxjs/toolkit/skills/manage-server-data/adopt-rtk-query/SKILL.md` and `model-redux-state/design-state-ownership/SKILL.md`.

## Components

- Function components with named exports, one per file named after it. A screen's components, hooks, and tests sit beside it under `src/pages/` and move to `src/components/` or `src/hooks/` only when a second screen needs them; import from the defining file (no `index.ts` barrels, no `export *`); hooks are named after a use case (`useNotesFilter`), never `useMount`/`usePrevious`, and are created only when a second caller exists.
- Props are an explicit `interface` on `function X({ a }: Props)` (no `React.FC`); `ref` is a plain prop (no `forwardRef`), providers are `<Ctx value>` (no `.Provider`), defaults are parameter defaults (no `defaultProps`, no `propTypes`), the only class is an error boundary. `unknown` at every boundary (`JSON.parse`, `localStorage`, `error.data`, `URLSearchParams`, `catch`) narrowed by a guard; `as` only to name what a guard proved, never to silence tsc. UI state is a discriminated union whose `switch` ends in a `never` default, never parallel booleans; `satisfies` for literal maps.
- `useEffect` synchronises with something outside React (a subscription, focus, `setupListeners`); a `setState` called synchronously inside an effect means the state should not exist (compute it in render) or the update belongs in the event handler; reset a subtree with `key={id}`, not an effect; never `biome-ignore` `useExhaustiveDependencies` (use `useEffectEvent` or restructure). The React Compiler memoizes (ADR 0021): no `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `memo` without a profiler measurement in the change; `"use no memo"` only with a comment naming the rule violation being worked around; fix the cause first (state lifted too high, components defined inside components).
- Markup is semantic: `<button type="button">`, `<Link>` for navigation, `<label>` wrapping every input, headings in order, `useId()` for any `htmlFor`/`aria-describedby` pair. On route change focus moves to the screen's `<h1 tabIndex={-1}>` and the page name is announced (the `RouteFocus` component in `App.tsx`); each screen renders its own `<title>`; modals are native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` with an explicit close button. Tests and E2E locate elements by role and label, so unsemantic markup fails them.
- Text goes through `t("screen.key")` with keys namespaced by screen in `src/i18n/locales/en.json`, added in the same change (split into per-feature namespaces past about 300 keys); plurals use `_one`/`_other` with `{ count }`; `<Trans>` only for sentences with inline elements; sentences are never concatenated. API times are UTC ISO-8601, displayed through `formatDateTime(iso)` from `src/i18n/format.ts` (an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` on `i18n.language`) inside `<time dateTime={iso}>`; date-fns is for arithmetic and relative time, `TZDate` for an explicit zone; numbers and currency through `Intl.NumberFormat`.
- Styling is Tailwind utilities in `className`, values from `@theme` in `src/index.css`: no arbitrary colours, spacing, or type sizes that exist in the theme, no off-scale integers (`mt-17`), no `@apply`, no string-built class names (`bg-${c}-500` does not compile; data-driven values go through `style={{ "--x": v }}` and `bg-(--x)`); class order is layout, box, typography, colour, then state and responsive variants. Repeated markup becomes a component, not a shared class. No CSS modules, static inline `style`, CSS-in-JS, or component library without an ADR.
- Forms: inputs are uncontrolled with `name` attributes read via `new FormData(event.currentTarget)` on submit unless a value drives rendering; native `required`/`type`/`minLength`/`autocomplete` come first; on success navigate or `form.reset()` and announce in a `role="status"` region.

## Tests

- Vitest and Testing Library, `X.test.tsx` beside `X.tsx`, rendered through `renderWithProviders(ui, { preloadedState, route })` from `src/test/` (fresh store, `MemoryRouter`, i18n); interact with `const user = userEvent.setup()` and await every call; query by role, label, and text with jest-dom matchers (`toBeInTheDocument`, `toBeDisabled`, `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage`, `toHaveFocus`), never `toBeDefined()`; `find*` for async, no empty `waitFor`, no snapshots, `getByTestId` only with a comment saying why.
- The network is mocked only with MSW handlers in `src/test/handlers.ts` (`onUnhandledRequest: "error"`); never mock generated hooks, `react-redux`, or `react-router`; prove invalidation by asserting what the user sees after the refetch; one test per visible state of a screen (loading, error, empty, data, validation error, pending submit).
- Anything that crosses into the backend is a Playwright journey in `../e2e` (its AGENTS.md has the rules).
